feedback.end: Brackets should be used when the extra information is not very important.

instruction.text: Select the extra information that has been added to the sentence.

atoms.b: Tom, ((who I went to school with)), works for one of the biggest companies in the UK.

feedback.end: Commas are used in more formal writing. They should only be used if there are not already too many commas used in the sentence.

instruction.text: Select the extra information that has been added to the sentence.

atoms.b: Stella’s dog — ((a Jack Russel Terrier)) — enjoys playing fetch.

feedback.end: Dashes are used in more informal writing. They are used to make the extra information stand out.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that uses brackets correctly.

atoms.a: Rae is going to the rugby match tomorrow, Gwent Dragons verses Cardiff Blues, and she is very excited.
b: ++Rae is going to the rugby match tomorrow (Gwent Dragons verses Cardiff Blues), and she is very excited.
(Rae is going to the rugby match tomorrow) Gwent Dragons verses Cardiff Blues, and she is very excited.

atoms.a: The snow storm, not forecast in the weather report, meant that we had to cancel our day trip.
b: ++The snow storm (not forecast in the weather report) meant that we had to cancel our day trip
The snow storm not (forecast) in the weather report meant that we had to cancel our day trip.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that uses commas correctly.

atoms.a: The train, which travelled from London to Manchester, was quite busy.
b: ++The train, which travelled from London to Manchester, was quite busy.
The train which travelled, from London to Manchester was, quite busy.

atoms.a: My mum, who grew up in France, can speak fluent French.
b: ++My mum, who grew up in France, can speak fluent French.
My mum who grew up in France, can speak, fluent French.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that uses dashes correctly.

atoms.a: Rakesh, whose mum owns a business, wants to be a successful business owner when he is older.
b: ++Rakesh — whose mum owns a business — wants to be a successful business owner when he is older.
Rakesh whose mum owns a business — wants to be a successful business owner when he is older—.

atoms.a: Ellie, who didn’t like dogs, said hello to her neighbour’s poodle.
b: ++Ellie — who didn’t like dogs — said hello to her neighbour’s poodle.
Ellie who didn’t like dogs — said hello — to her neighbour’s poodle.
